title: Session 2: Data Models, Relational Algebra, and Normalization — SQL Server

questions.questionText: A group of conceptual tools that describes data, its relationships, semantics, and consistency constraints is called a:
questions.explanation: This is the definition of a data model.

questions.questionText: The process of applying an appropriate data model to data in order to organize and structure it is called:
questions.explanation: Data modeling applies a data model to the data.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT one of the three broad steps of data modeling?
questions.explanation: The three steps are conceptual, logical, and physical data modeling.

questions.questionText: The E-R model belongs to which classification of data models?
questions.explanation: The E-R model is an object-based logical model.

questions.questionText: A real-world object that exists physically and is distinguishable from other objects is a(n):
questions.explanation: Examples include employee, department, student, and vehicle.

questions.questionText: Features that an entity has, and that help distinguish one entity from another, are called:
questions.explanation: Attributes describe an entity, e.g., roll_number, name, stream.

questions.questionText: A collection of similar entities, such as all employees of an organization, is called a(n):
questions.explanation: All the employees collectively form the employee entity set.

questions.questionText: The JOIN operation is an enhancement of which relational operator?
questions.explanation: JOIN performs a selection on the product of tables.

questions.questionText: A manager and a team member both belong to the Employee entity set, and the team member 'works for' the manager. This is a:
questions.explanation: Relationships between entities of the same entity set are self-relationships.

questions.questionText: 'An employee belongs to a department' is an example of a:
questions.explanation: It links entities from two different entity sets.

questions.questionText: An employee works in the accounts department at the regional branch. This relationship involving Employee, Department, and Location is:
questions.explanation: A ternary relationship exists between three entity sets.

questions.questionText: Every vehicle has a unique registration, and no two vehicles share one. This mapping cardinality is:
questions.explanation: One vehicle maps to exactly one registration.

questions.questionText: A customer can own more than one vehicle. The mapping cardinality from customer to vehicle is:
questions.explanation: One customer is associated with one or more vehicles.

questions.questionText: Many vehicles are manufactured by a single company. From vehicle to manufacturer, the cardinality is:
questions.explanation: Many vehicles map to one manufacturer.

questions.questionText: Customers and bank accounts (including joint accounts) have which mapping cardinality?
questions.explanation: A customer can have many accounts and an account can have many customers.

questions.questionText: An attribute that can uniquely define an entity in an entity set is called a:
questions.explanation: For example, enrollment_number in the Student Details table.

questions.questionText: Entity sets that do not have enough attributes to establish a primary key are called:
questions.explanation: The Assignment entity set is a weak entity set in the book's example.

questions.questionText: In E-R diagrams, a multi-valued attribute is drawn as a:
questions.explanation: Derived attributes use dashed ellipses; multi-valued use double-line ellipses.

questions.questionText: An address made up of street, area, and similar parts is an example of a:
questions.explanation: A composite attribute contains two or more attributes with independent meanings.

questions.questionText: An attribute whose value is entirely dependent on another attribute, such as age from date of birth, is:
questions.explanation: Derived attributes are shown with dashed ellipses.

questions.questionText: What is the first step in constructing an E-R diagram?
options: Gather all the data that must be modeled
questions.correctAnswer: Gather all the data that must be modeled
questions.explanation: The steps begin with gathering the data to be modeled.

questions.questionText: Adding a new employee who has not been assigned to any project, forcing blank project columns, causes a(n):
questions.explanation: Anomalies created by such insertions are insertion anomalies.

questions.questionText: A salary change for John that must be reflected in every project row he appears in illustrates a(n):
questions.explanation: Updating all occurrences is the updating anomaly problem.

questions.questionText: Normalization is best defined as:
options: Adding redundant data to improve speed
questions.explanation: It reduces redundancy and helps maintain integrity.

questions.questionText: To achieve first normal form, table columns must have:
questions.explanation: 1NF also requires identifying key attributes and creating separate tables for related data.

questions.questionText: A table is in second normal form if it meets 1NF and has no:
questions.explanation: 2NF also requires tables to be related through foreign keys.

questions.questionText: Third normal form requires that tables have no:
questions.explanation: A non-key attribute must not be determined by another non-key attribute.

questions.questionText: In the Employee Details table, Salary depends on Grade rather than Emp_No. To reach 3NF, the table is split into Employee Details and:
questions.explanation: This removes the transitive dependency.

questions.questionText: Deliberately introducing minor redundancy into a normalized database to improve performance is called:
questions.explanation: It reduces the need for complex, frequent joins.

questions.questionText: Which relational operator extracts rows that satisfy a given condition and is denoted by sigma?
questions.explanation: PROJECT (pi) picks columns; SELECT (sigma) picks rows.

questions.questionText: An entity set is a collection of similar entities.
questions.explanation: E.g., all employees form the employee entity set.

questions.questionText: A ternary relationship exists between exactly two entity sets.
questions.explanation: A ternary relationship involves three entity sets.

questions.questionText: A weak entity set has enough attributes to establish a primary key.
questions.explanation: That describes a strong entity set.

questions.questionText: A derived attribute's value is entirely dependent on another attribute.
questions.explanation: Age derived from birth date is the example.

questions.questionText: An unnormalized table can suffer from insertion, deletion, and updating anomalies.
questions.explanation: These drawbacks motivate normalization.

questions.questionText: Second normal form requires that there be no partial dependencies.
questions.explanation: The tables should also be related through foreign keys.

questions.questionText: Denormalization completely eliminates redundancy from a database.
questions.explanation: It introduces minor redundancy to improve performance.

questions.questionText: The PRODUCT operator combines each record of the first table with all records of the second table.
questions.explanation: It generates all possible combinations.

questions.questionText: The INTERSECT operator returns data that holds true in one table but not in the other.
questions.explanation: That is DIFFERENCE. INTERSECT returns data true in all tables.

questions.questionText: In the DIVIDE operation, the attributes of the divisor table should be a subset of those of the dividend table.
questions.explanation: The result lacks the divisor's attributes.

questions.questionText: A ____________ attribute can be broken into smaller attributes that each have independent meaning.
questions.explanation: Address (street, area) is an example of a composite attribute.

questions.questionText: ____________ is the process of removing unwanted redundancy and dependencies from tables.
questions.explanation: Normalization reduces redundancy and maintains data integrity.

questions.questionText: The ____________ operator, denoted by the Greek letter pi, displays only the required columns.
questions.explanation: PROJECT selects columns; SELECT (sigma) selects rows.

questions.questionText: A relationship between entities of the same entity set is called a ____________ relationship.
questions.explanation: E.g., manager and team member within the Employee entity set.

questions.questionText: In third normal form, every non-key attribute should be determined only by the ____________ attribute.
questions.explanation: This eliminates transitive dependencies.

questions.questionText: Emp_No and Project_Id together form a ____________ primary key in the Employee Project Details table.
questions.explanation: Two or more attributes combine to uniquely identify a record.

questions.questionText: The ____________ operator, symbolized by '-', returns data true in one table and not the other.
questions.explanation: DIFFERENCE returns records present in the first table but absent in the second.

questions.questionText: An individual's telephone numbers are an example of a ____________ attribute.
questions.explanation: A person may have one or more phone numbers.

questions.questionText: An E-R diagram is a ____________ representation of the E-R model.
questions.explanation: Symbols represent entities, attributes, and relationships.

questions.questionText: Codd presented the first three normal forms (1NF, 2NF, 3NF) in the year ____________.
questions.explanation: E. F. Codd introduced 1NF, 2NF, and 3NF in 1972; 4NF and 5NF came later.
